papers.title_en: Evidence for the binary nature of the long-period radio transient ASKAP/DART J1832-0911
papers.authors: Csanád Horváth, Natasha Hurley-Walker, Ziteng Wang, Andrew Zic, Emil Lenc
papers.evidence: 由射电数据推断长周期射电暂现源的双星本质
papers.tldr: 长周期射电暂现源可在分钟至小时尺度重复脉冲，近年多被证认为白矮星与低质量主序星组成的双星。本文利用两年射电观测分析迄今最亮的 ASKAP/DART J1832-0911，提出它或为轨道更致密的白矮星系统。其脉冲含准周期成分并逐日逐月演化，偏振、RM、谱指数随相位系统变化，异于脉冲星与磁星。超致密异步极模型可解释脉冲形态、RM 变化与周期性 X 射线，虽未确证双星，但给出可检验预言。
papers.abstract_en: Long-period transients are a class of periodic pulsed radio source repeating on the minute to hour timescale. Recently, an increasing number of them are being identified as binary systems, specifically white dwarfs with low-mass main-sequence companions. In this work we analyse the most luminous long-period transient discovered to date, ASKAP/DART J1832-0911, with two years of radio data, and propose that it, too, may be a white dwarf system, although in a far more compact orbit than the aforementioned. The pulses are composed of quasi-periodic components which evolve in a systematic way over days and months. The source is highly linearly or elliptically polarised and its brightness enabled very high signal-to-noise measurement of the time-resolved Faraday rotation measure, which was found to vary across pulse phase. The linear polarisation position angle, circular polarised fraction, and spectral index also varied systematically in ways not typical of pulsars and magnetars. We show that an ultra-compact asynchronous polar explains much of the phenomenology of ASKAP/DART J1832-0911, in particular the evolution of the pulse morphology, rotation measure variation, and periodic X-ray emission, although we cannot conclusively prove a binary nature. However, our model makes testable predictions.
